definitions.gloss: buying books and leaving them unread; piling up unread books
definitions.explanation: The habit of acquiring books but letting them pile up without reading them. A playful compound blending {積|つ}む (to pile up) with {読|どく} (reading).

examples.japanese: {積|つ}ん{読|どく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦どんどん→どんどん：01261_dondon⟧⟦{増|ふ}える→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: My pile of unread books keeps growing.

examples.japanese: ⟦また→また：00969_mata⟧{本|ほん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}って→買う：00489_kau⟧しまった。{積|つ}ん{読|どく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{止|と}まらない→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧。
examples.english: I bought another book. I can't stop piling up unread ones.

examples.japanese: ⟦{本棚|ほんだな}→本棚：04489_hondana⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{半分|はんぶん}→半分：02938_hanbun⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{積|つ}ん{読|どく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{本|ほん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{埋|う}まっている→埋まる：01897_umaru⟧。
examples.english: Half my bookshelf is filled with books I've bought but never read.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
A playful portmanteau of ⟦{積|つ}む→積む：02294_tsumu⟧ (to pile up) and {読|どく} (reading, from ⟦{読書|どくしょ}→読書：03484_dokusho⟧). The ん connects the two elements, mimicking the sound of ⟦{積|つ}んで→積む：02294_tsumu⟧おく (to leave piled up). The word dates to the Meiji era.

USAGE:
Used both as a noun ({積|つ}ん{読|どく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{本|ほん}, unread books) and with ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ ({積|つ}ん{読|どく}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧). The word carries a self-deprecating, humorous tone — book lovers use it to describe their own habit. It has been borrowed into English as "tsundoku."

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{精読|せいどく}→精読：15982_seidoku⟧ (close reading)
- ⟦{多読|たどく}→多読：15981_tadoku⟧ (extensive reading)
- ⟦{読書|どくしょ}→読書：03484_dokusho⟧ (reading books)
